title: Injury Prediction in Competitive Runners With Machine Learning
authors: Lovdal SS, Den Hartigh RJR, Azzopardi G
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: 74 high-level middle- and long-distance runners with detailed training logs over 7 years
findings: Bagged XGBoost models on a daily time series (previous 7 days, 10 features/day mixing GPS-watch data and subjective exertion and success) reached average ROC AUC 0.724.
A weekly approach (22 aggregate features, 3-week window) reached average AUC 0.678.
The authors report the system predicts a sizable portion of injuries, particularly with data from the days preceding injury, and suggest ML could help tailor training programs.
limitations: 74 runners from one new data set; modest AUC (0.68-0.72) is the verifier's assessment that it is insufficient to drive decisions; no external or recreational validation in abstract. The researcher's claim of a published erratum could not be confirmed (Crossref/PubMed show none) and was removed. Study type (retrospective ML on logs) inferred from the abstract.
implications: ML injury-risk output at this accuracy must not drive automatic plan changes; at most a non-alarming heads-up, with plans governed by explicit conservative rules.
Capture subjective daily data (perceived exertion, session success) alongside GPS metrics.
Prefer daily-resolution features over weekly aggregates if an exploratory indicator is built.

verification.notes: Crossref and PubMed XML: title, IJSPP, print 2021-10 (e-pub 2021-04-29), first author Lovdal (Lövdal) match. Abstract re-read. Design reclassified prospective-cohort to other; erratum claim removed (unverified).
